We propose a $186,000 base salary and a $12,000 signing bonus for an April 5, 2027 start. Mara would own Trestle Freight’s internal security platform, set its technical roadmap, and lead the platform work for the July audit.

For the first 12 weeks, we’d like Mara on site one day each week. If fewer trips work better, we can group that time into two three-day visits per month, with Trestle covering travel. We propose business-hours incident coverage for Mara, with training the after-hours escalation partner included in her onboarding.

If Mara can start March 22, we can increase the signing bonus to $18,000 at the same base. Those two weeks would give her more time with the platform team before audit preparation. Which start date and travel schedule work best for Mara, and what would she need clarified or changed to recommend the package?

June 1, 2027 is Mara’s earliest start. She can recommend that date at a $186,000 base with a $12,000 signing bonus payable on her first payroll to replace the vest she would forfeit. If Trestle prefers to forgo the bonus, she can start July 1 at the same base. The June option gives her a month with the team before the July audit.

Mara can commit to the two three-day visits per month you offered for the first 12 weeks, scheduled in advance with Trestle covering travel and lodging. After that, she proposes working remotely with any on-site days grouped into at most two mutually scheduled visits per month.

For the written offer, please confirm that Mara will own the platform’s security architecture, including design decisions and the technical roadmap. With a June start, who will own audit preparation through May, and which July deliverables would Mara inherit at handoff?

Mara can train the after-hours partner during business hours. Her acceptance depends on staffed after-hours coverage from day one, including while that partner is in training or unavailable. Can Trestle identify the primary and backup responders and confirm in writing that Mara’s incident coverage is limited to business hours?

Trestle can recommend the **June 1, 2027 start at a $186,000 annual base salary, with a $12,000 signing bonus payable on Mara’s first payroll**. We’ll put the following terms in the written offer.

- **Platform ownership.** Mara will own the internal security platform’s security architecture, make its technical design decisions, and set its technical roadmap.
- **Audit handoff.** Trestle will designate an audit lead who owns preparation through May 31 and remains responsible for the overall July submission. On June 1, that lead will give Mara the platform evidence inventory, open findings, owners, and deadlines. For July, Mara will own validation of the platform evidence, the technical remediation plan for open platform findings, and responses to auditors’ platform questions. Trestle will identify the audit lead and provide an itemized list of those deliverables and due dates before Mara accepts.
- **Site visits.** For the first 12 weeks, Mara will make two three-day visits per month, scheduled in advance. Afterward, she will work remotely, with any on-site days grouped into at most two mutually scheduled visits per month. Trestle will cover travel and lodging for those visits throughout.
- **Incident coverage.** Mara’s incident duties and her training of the escalation partner will take place during business hours only. Trestle will staff primary and backup after-hours coverage from day one, including while the partner is training or unavailable. Mara will have no after-hours paging, standby, or fallback duty.

The responder assignments still need confirmation. Before asking Mara to accept, Trestle will name the primary and backup responders in writing and confirm who covers each role during training and absences.

These terms work for Mara. Please send the written offer with the audit lead’s name, the itemized July platform deliverables and their due dates, and the names of the primary and backup after-hours responders, specifying who covers each role during training and absences. Once Mara confirms the deadlines are workable from June 1 and both after-hours roles are covered from day one, I can recommend acceptance.

Trestle’s written offer is a **June 1, 2027 start, a $186,000 annual base salary, and a $12,000 signing bonus payable on Mara’s first payroll**. The audit dates below are proposed. The audit lead and after-hours staffing assignments still require internal confirmation. We’ll keep acceptance open until Mara has reviewed the confirmed dates and named roster.

Mara will own the internal security platform’s security architecture, its technical design decisions, and its technical roadmap. For the first 12 weeks, she will make two three-day site visits per month, scheduled in advance. After that, she will work remotely, with any on-site days grouped into at most two mutually scheduled visits per month. Trestle will cover travel and lodging throughout.

**July audit.** Trestle’s designated audit lead will own preparation through May 31 and retain responsibility for the overall submission. On June 1, the lead will hand Mara the evidence inventory, open findings, owners, and deadlines. We propose the following schedule for Mara’s platform work, subject to confirmation against the auditor’s calendar.

| Proposed due date | Platform deliverable |
|---|---|
| July 2 | Return the validated platform evidence inventory to the audit lead, identifying missing evidence and who can supply it. |
| July 9 | Deliver a technical remediation plan for each open platform finding, with a proposed owner and target date. |
| July 16 | Deliver technical responses to the platform questions received by July 9. The audit lead and Mara will agree on deadlines for later questions when they arrive. |

**Incident coverage.** Mara’s incident duties and partner training will take place during business hours only. She will have no after-hours paging, standby, or fallback duty. From day one, Trestle will assign two trained responders to each after-hours shift. While the escalation partner is training, two qualified responders will hold the primary and backup roles. If either is absent, Trestle will assign a qualified replacement so both roles remain staffed.

The outstanding offer details are the audit lead’s name, the confirmed deliverable dates, and the names of the primary, backup, and relief responders, including who fills each role during training and absences. Trestle will provide those details in writing before requesting Mara’s acceptance.

The proposed July 2, 9, and 16 deadlines look workable for Mara with the June 1 handoff and the July 9 cutoff for auditor questions. I’ll hold my recommendation until Mara has reviewed the confirmed dates, the audit lead’s name, and the written roster showing who covers both after-hours roles from day one, including during training and absences.

Ivo can reserve a guaranteed block of 50 design days for $42,500, with a 30% deposit ($12,750) paid within two business days of signing. The remaining payments would be 30% on delivery of the concept package and 40% on delivery of the fabrication-ready design package.

The scope covers concept design, accessibility design, and fabrication-ready documentation for the traveling exhibit, with two rounds of consolidated revisions. Additional revisions require written approval at $900 per day. Fabrication supervision is a separate engagement at $900 per day, subject to Ivo’s availability and dates agreed in advance. The agreement would let Ivo use photographs cleared for publication in their portfolio after the public opening.

If Hearth needs flexibility on the number of days, Ivo can work at $900 per day and reserve the days Hearth commits to at signing. When does the fabrication slot expire, when does the fabricator need the final package, and can Hearth meet the deposit timing for the discounted block?

Hearth proposes a fixed fee of $42,500 for 46 guaranteed working days, including two on-site installation days. We can meet the two-business-day payment timing with a 20% deposit of $8,500. We propose three further payments on delivery:

- $12,750 for the concept package.
- $12,750 for the fabrication-ready package, including editable native files and a documented accessible alternate layout.
- $8,500 on completion of the two installation days and delivery of the final files reflecting any changes agreed on site.

The two consolidated revision rounds would be included. The installation days would cover design coordination and accessibility checks with the installer. Any additional revisions or fabrication supervision would require a written change order at $900 per day. Would the 46-day guarantee work with site travel included? If travel needs a separate allowance, please quote a capped amount.

Ivo would retain copyright and grant Hearth a perpetual, nonexclusive license to fabricate, exhibit, tour, repair and adapt the exhibit, including sharing editable files with fabricators and host venues for those purposes. Ivo could use cleared photographs in their portfolio once the touring venue opens, scheduled for two months after launch. Hearth would confirm the opening and photo clearance in writing.

The slot expiry and final-file deadline still need confirmation from the fabricator. What is the latest date Ivo can hold the block pending signature, and what lead time is needed from kickoff to fabrication-ready delivery, including both review rounds? With those dates, we can put the concept delivery, Hearth’s review deadlines, final handoff and two installation days into the agreement.

Ivo can agree to a fixed fee of $42,500 for 46 guaranteed working days, including 44 design days and two on-site installation days for design coordination and accessibility checks. We propose reimbursing preapproved travel at cost, capped at $1,500 total for one round trip covering both installation days. That assumes the days are consecutive at one venue and travel can fit around them. Can you confirm the venue city and tentative dates?

We can meet Hearth at a 25% deposit and keep the four delivery milestones:

- $10,625 within two business days of signing.
- $12,750 on delivery of the concept package.
- $14,875 on delivery of the fabrication-ready package, including editable native files and a documented accessible alternate layout.
- $4,250 after the two installation days and delivery of the final files reflecting agreed on-site changes.

If Hearth postpones installation by more than 30 days from the agreed dates, the final installment would become due on day 30, with Ivo still responsible for the two rescheduled days and final file updates. The design fee includes two consolidated revision rounds. Additional revisions and fabrication supervision require a written change order at $900 per day, with any supervision dates agreed in advance.

The proposed copyright and license terms work for Ivo. For portfolio use, we propose that Hearth clear a selection of photographs in writing for use from the first public opening. If Hearth needs an embargo through the first touring venue opening, we can agree to a fixed release date in the agreement so a tour delay does not extend the embargo.

Ivo can hold the block for five business days from this proposal pending signature, with the deposit due within two business days after signing. Please allow 11 weeks from kickoff to fabrication-ready delivery, including both review rounds, assuming Hearth provides the exhibit content, venue constraints and fabricator requirements at kickoff and returns consolidated feedback within five business days per round. Ivo can deliver the concept package by the end of week three. Once the fabricator confirms the slot expiry and handoff deadline, we can work backward to set the kickoff, both review deadlines and the final handoff date.

Hearth can commit to the $42,500 fixed fee for 44 design days and two consecutive installation days at one venue. We accept reimbursement of preapproved travel at cost, up to $1,500 total for one round trip. The venue city and installation dates are still unconfirmed. We’ll include them in the schedule for both parties to approve before travel is booked.

**The deposit must stay at 20%.** We can move the $2,125 difference to the concept payment and accept Ivo’s proposed 10% final installment. The payments would be:

- **$8,500** within two business days of signing.
- **$14,875** on delivery of the concept package.
- **$14,875** on delivery of the fabrication-ready package, including editable native files and the documented accessible alternate layout.
- **$4,250** after both installation days and delivery of the files reflecting agreed on-site changes. If Hearth postpones installation by more than 30 days, we accept payment on day 30 after the originally agreed installation date. Both installation days and the file updates would remain covered by the fee.

Hearth accepts the two consolidated revision rounds, written change orders at $900 per day for additional revisions or fabrication supervision, and the agreed copyright and license terms. For portfolio use, Hearth can clear selected photos in writing in advance. The sponsor requires the embargo to run through the **actual first touring venue opening**, expected two months after launch. Hearth will confirm that opening in writing the day it occurs so Ivo can publish the precleared photos immediately. An earlier release would require the sponsor’s written clearance.

We accept concept delivery by the end of week three and fabrication-ready delivery by the end of week eleven, with Hearth supplying the agreed inputs at kickoff and consolidated feedback within five business days per round. During the five-business-day hold, Hearth will seek confirmation of the slot expiry and handoff deadline from the fabricator so we can date the kickoff, both reviews and handoff before signing. Can Ivo accept the revised payment amounts and the touring-opening release on that basis?

Ivo accepts the revised payment schedule of $8,500 within two business days of signing, $14,875 on concept delivery, $14,875 on fabrication-ready delivery, and $4,250 after the two installation days and delivery of the updated files. The agreed 30-day postponement provision applies to the final installment.

Ivo also accepts the embargo through the actual first touring venue opening. Hearth will clear selected photos in writing in advance and confirm the opening in writing that day so Ivo can publish the cleared photos immediately. Any earlier release requires the sponsor’s written clearance.

Once the fabricator confirms the slot expiry and handoff deadline, please send both dates so we can finalize the kickoff, review deadlines and handoff schedule within the five-business-day hold. The installation dates and venue can be approved by both parties before travel is booked.

Caldera proposes that Dev begin the overlap on September 1 and take over as director on January 1. We propose an annual salary rate of $138,000 during the overlap and $155,000 from January 1, contingent on formal approval of the director appointment. Can both boards approve the January appointment before the overlap begins, so Dev has a firm commitment before making relocation arrangements?

The incumbent would remain director through December 31 and retain overall operational accountability. Dev would lead day-to-day operations and could receive procurement authority immediately for purchases up to $60,000. The Caldera board would retain personnel decisions through December 31. We propose that the incumbent lead introductions and brief Dev on open contracts, budget commitments and staffing matters. Dev would prepare the January operating plan, and both would review outstanding handoff items with the board in December.

What date could Dev begin working on site, and when could Dev complete a permanent move? Caldera could cover temporary lodging, training, or a combination up to $8,000 total. Which allocation would best support Dev’s transition?

We can take a September 1 on-site start and January 1 director appointment to Dev’s board. Dev can commute in scheduled blocks from September through December and complete the permanent move after the school term ends in December, ahead of January 1. Before the overlap starts, we’d ask both boards to approve the transition and Caldera’s board to adopt a resolution appointing Dev effective January 1. Can Caldera approve the appointment on that basis before September 1?

Dev can accept the $138,000 annualized overlap rate if Caldera applies the full $8,000 to temporary lodging and guarantees the $155,000 rate beginning January 1, even if the appointment is delayed. Any required training would come from Caldera’s operating budget. Let’s agree on the on-site blocks and confirm lodging costs before either board votes.

During the overlap, the incumbent would retain overall operational accountability, and the board would retain formal personnel decisions. Dev would lead day-to-day operations, including directing crews, changing shift assignments, calling in coverage, and authorizing purchases up to $60,000. For outages, Dev would have authority to take immediate safety and service-restoration actions. The incumbent would handle decisions beyond Dev’s delegated authority, with a named backup and a written escalation process. Dev would be accountable for decisions within that delegation.

The incumbent would lead introductions and brief Dev on open contracts, budget commitments, and staffing. Dev would prepare the January operating plan. At the December board review, they would record any open handoff items with an owner and due date. The appointment resolution would make January 1 the title trigger, with remaining handoff items carried into the operating plan.

If the appointment slips, Caldera would document the reason, name the person who holds director accountability, and set a firm decision date no later than January 31. Dev’s delegated authority and $155,000 rate would continue. If Caldera can’t confirm the January 1 appointment by the December review, Dev can defer the permanent move and Caldera would cover lodging for agreed on-site blocks beyond the overlap cap. If the appointment is still unresolved on January 31, Dev can end the interim assignment without a repayment obligation or agree in writing to a defined extension.

Caldera can put a binding January 1 appointment resolution to its board before September 1. We propose making both boards’ approvals and delivery of Caldera’s signed resolution conditions for Dev to start the overlap. The resolution would set the director salary at **$155,000 effective January 1**, with no second vote required in December. Once the board approves the appointment, an administrative delay in implementing it would leave that pay date intact. Caldera can commit to the January rate on that basis.

For the September 1 through December 31 overlap, Caldera offers **$138,000 annualized** and will reserve the full **$8,000 for temporary lodging**, paying actual agreed costs up to that amount. We propose two consecutive on-site workweeks beginning September 1, followed by alternating on-site and remote workweeks through December. Dev would lead daily operations during remote weeks, with an identified on-site lead for each shift. Before the votes, let’s settle the block dates, including the December review, and obtain a lodging quote covering taxes and fees. If the quote exceeds $8,000, we can adjust the blocks or accommodation before either side commits. Caldera would provide required orientation during paid work time using existing staff and resources. Dev would arrange the permanent move after the school term and before January 1, subject to the December confirmation below.

Caldera accepts the proposed operational delegation. Dev may direct crews, adjust shifts, call in coverage, authorize purchases up to $60,000, and take immediate safety and service-restoration action during outages. Dev is accountable for those decisions. The incumbent retains director accountability through December 31, and the board retains formal personnel decisions. Before September 1, Caldera will name the incumbent’s backup and issue written escalation instructions covering outages, purchases above Dev’s limit, and personnel matters.

The incumbent will lead introductions and brief Dev on contracts, budget commitments, and staffing. Dev will prepare the January operating plan. At the December review, they will record an owner and due date for each open item and carry it into the plan. Those items will not delay the appointment.

If Caldera identifies a delay at the December review, Dev may defer the move. Caldera will document the reason, identify who holds director accountability, continue Dev’s delegated authority and approved January pay rate, and set a decision date no later than January 31. Once the lodging allowance is exhausted, we propose remote work for any extension unless both sides agree in writing on a funded on-site arrangement. If the appointment remains unresolved on January 31, Dev may end the interim assignment without repaying lodging costs or agree in writing to an extension with a fixed end date.

Would the proposed rotation and remote-work fallback work for Dev? Please identify any dates Dev needs on site or at home so we can price the lodging and put the same calendar before both boards.

The rotation and remote-work fallback work for Dev. For the September 2027 start, please price lodging for these proposed on-site blocks, including taxes and fees:

- September 1–3, 6–10, and 20–24
- October 4–8 and 18–22
- November 1–5, 15–19, and November 29–December 3
- December 13–17, with the board handoff review on December 14

Dev would work remotely on the other workdays, including December 20–31, with a designated on-site lead for each shift. That keeps the final two weeks available for the move after the school term ends, subject to Caldera confirming at the December review that the January 1 appointment is on track. If the lodging quote exceeds $8,000, let’s settle any changes to the calendar or accommodation before the boards vote.

Both boards’ approvals and delivery of Caldera’s signed January 1 appointment resolution would be conditions for the September 1 start. The board materials should include the agreed operational delegation and state that the $155,000 annual rate takes effect January 1 and continues through any interim extension, even if Dev has yet to assume the title.

If succession slips, Dev may defer the move. Caldera would record the reason, name the person holding director accountability, and set a decision date no later than January 31. Dev’s delegated authority would continue, with remote work once the lodging allowance is exhausted unless both sides agree in writing to a funded on-site arrangement. If the appointment remains unresolved on January 31, Dev may end the interim assignment without repaying lodging costs or agree in writing to an extension with a fixed end date.

Caldera agrees to the proposed 2027 on-site blocks, the December 14 handoff review, and remote work on the remaining workdays, including December 20–31. Caldera will designate an on-site lead for each shift. At the December review, Caldera will confirm in writing whether the January 1, 2028 appointment is on track so Dev can finalize the move.

For lodging, arrival the evening before each block and checkout after the final shift would require **43 nights** across nine stays. The $8,000 allowance would cover an average of **$186.04 per night including taxes and fees**. That figure is a spending limit pending a property quote. Please confirm the worksite city or address and whether Dev plans to check out September 3 and return September 5. With those details, Caldera can obtain an itemized quote and settle any accommodation or calendar changes with Dev before either board votes.

Caldera will include the agreed delegation and delay provisions in the board materials. Both approvals and delivery of Caldera’s signed appointment resolution are conditions for the September 1 start at $138,000 annualized. Under that resolution, the $155,000 annual rate begins January 1, 2028 and continues through any agreed interim extension, including any period before Dev assumes the title.

Please price the 43-night itinerary with checkout after Dev’s September 3 shift and check-in on the evening of September 5. Caldera should confirm the assigned worksite address for each block so we can check the commute against the proposed lodging.

Please send the itemized quote, including taxes and fees, before either board votes. If the total exceeds $8,000, we can review other lodging options or agree on any calendar changes before finalizing the board materials.

Caldera will confirm the assigned worksite address for each block before pricing the nine stays. Those addresses are still pending, so a lodging quote is not yet available.

Before either board votes, Caldera will send a property quote for all 43 nights, with checkout after the September 3 shift and check-in on the evening of September 5. For each stay, we’ll include the lodging and worksite addresses, estimated commute, room charges, taxes, fees, and total. If the combined quote exceeds $8,000, Caldera will review alternatives with Dev and agree on any lodging or calendar changes before submitting the plan for approval.

Noor proposes joining Finch three days a week, moving to four on March 1, at a full-time equivalent salary of $125,000. That comes to $75,000 annualized for three days and $100,000 for four. We can agree now on what the fourth day will cover and use a late-February review to set priorities for the expanded schedule.

Noor’s current editorial project has nine months left and would continue independently. Its data and unfinished articles would stay with the project. Noor would disclose any overlap in coverage and recuse from Finch decisions about the outside project or its work, with a designated Finch editor handling those decisions.

Noor would have final say on methods corrections within the desk’s remit, with Finch retaining its usual authority over other editorial decisions. We’re flexible on title and the timing of the review. Would Finch be comfortable committing to the March increase at signing, with the review focused on how to use the added time?

Finch can commit at signing to Noor moving from three days a week to four on March 1. The late-February review would set priorities for the fourth day. We need the desk to accept submissions four days a week starting in December, so we propose that a Finch deputy cover the fourth intake day through February.

If Noor takes responsibility for training the deputy, we can offer $128,000 full-time equivalent, prorated to $76,800 annualized at three days and $102,400 at four. Before December intake opens, Noor and the deputy would document how the deputy logs and triages submissions, what gets escalated to the duty editor that day, and what Noor reviews on returning. Would Noor take on the training and review the deputy’s intake decisions during the first month?

The outside project can continue for its remaining nine months on the terms you outlined. Its data, drafts, and working files would stay separate from Finch’s materials. Noor would disclose coverage overlap and recuse from Finch decisions involving the project or its work, with a designated Finch editor handling those decisions.

Noor would lead the technical assessment and recommend the wording of methods corrections. If a correction is disputed, Noor would document the evidence and recommendation, and a second editor with relevant methods expertise would review it. The editor-in-chief would make the final publication decision, including whether and how to publish the correction, and record the rationale if it differs from Noor’s recommendation.

Noor accepts the $128,000 full-time equivalent, prorated to $76,800 at three days and $102,400 at four. We’re aligned on the March 1 increase, the late-February priority review, and the outside project terms. Noor can train the deputy, document the intake and escalation procedure together before December intake opens, and review the deputy’s first-month intake decisions on Noor’s scheduled days. The duty editor would handle same-day escalations on the deputy’s coverage day through February.

On corrections, Noor can agree to a second review by an editor with relevant methods expertise and a written record of how disagreements are resolved. Noor needs final say on whether the evidence warrants a methods correction and on the technical accuracy of its wording. Finch’s editor-in-chief would retain authority over timing, placement, and nontechnical edits, with discretion to pause publication for a specific legal or standards concern and document the reason. For matters from which Noor is recused, the designated Finch editor would take Noor’s place. Can Finch agree to that division of authority?

Finch can give Noor lead responsibility for determining whether the evidence warrants a methods correction and for drafting its technical wording. The editor-in-chief must retain final authority over whether and in what form Finch publishes a correction.

For a disputed correction, Noor would record the evidence and recommendation, and a second editor with relevant methods expertise would provide a written assessment. Before deciding, the editor-in-chief would give Noor and the reviewer a chance to assess any proposed change that affects the technical meaning. The editor-in-chief would record the rationale for declining a recommended correction or departing from Noor’s technical assessment, and document any specific legal or standards concern that delays publication. The designated Finch editor would take Noor’s place in this process when Noor is recused.

We’re aligned on compensation, the March 1 increase, the late-February priority review, the deputy’s December-through-February coverage and training, and the outside project terms. Can Noor agree to this corrections process so we can put the appointment in writing?

We’re aligned on the rest of the package. The remaining issue is who has final say on the technical finding when a correction is disputed.

Noor can agree to the written second review and to the editor-in-chief having final authority over whether and when Finch publishes. If the editor-in-chief declines or delays a correction, the rationale would go in the written record. If Finch publishes a methods correction, Noor would sign off on the technical finding and on any wording that changes its meaning. The designated Finch editor would exercise that authority when Noor is recused.

Can Finch put that distinction in the appointment letter?

Finch can put Noor’s authority over the desk’s technical finding in the appointment letter. Noor would sign off on the desk’s finding and on any wording presented as the desk’s conclusion. The editor-in-chief would retain final authority over whether, when, and in what form Finch publishes a correction.

If a disagreement remains after the written second review, the editor-in-chief would give Noor and the reviewer a chance to assess any proposed change in technical meaning. If Finch publishes a finding Noor does not endorse, it would publish it as Finch’s editorial determination and would not attribute it to Noor or the desk. The written record would preserve Noor’s finding, the second review, and the editor-in-chief’s rationale for departing from the finding or for declining or delaying publication. The designated Finch editor would take Noor’s place when Noor is recused.

Can Noor agree to that language for the appointment letter?

Noor can agree that the editor-in-chief has final say over whether and when Finch publishes a correction, and can publish a separate editorial note explaining any disagreement. Noor’s sign-off needs to apply to the technical finding in any methods correction Finch publishes, including one issued under Finch’s name. When Noor is recused, the designated Finch editor would provide that sign-off.

The written second review and decision record work for Noor. If the letter can make that distinction between a methods correction and an editorial note, we’re ready to finalize the appointment.

Finch can distinguish a methods correction from a separate editorial note in the appointment letter. We can make Noor’s sign-off the standard for the technical finding and any wording that changes its meaning. When Noor is recused, the designated Finch editor would have that role.

If Noor withholds sign-off after the written second review, the editor-in-chief could publish the disputed correction only if the second reviewer expressly endorses the technical finding and final wording in writing. The decision record would preserve both assessments and the editor-in-chief’s rationale. The editor-in-chief would retain final authority over whether and when to publish and could issue a separate editorial note explaining the disagreement.

Can Noor agree to that limited exception so we can finalize the appointment?

Noor can commit to reviewing the second editor’s written assessment promptly and recording the reasons if sign-off is still withheld. Sign-off on the technical finding and any wording that changes its meaning needs to stay with Noor, or with the designated Finch editor when Noor is recused.

The editor-in-chief would retain final authority over whether and when to publish an approved correction and could issue a separate editorial note explaining any unresolved disagreement. If Finch can put that process in the letter, Noor is ready to finalize on the other agreed terms.

Finch can write in the prompt review, the written reasons for withholding sign-off, and the option for a separate editorial note. We still need a path for the editor-in-chief to publish a disputed correction when the second methods editor expressly endorses the technical finding and final wording in writing. In that case, the decision record would preserve Noor’s reasons for withholding sign-off and the editor-in-chief’s rationale for publishing.

That limited exception is the remaining condition for Finch to finalize the appointment. If Noor’s sign-off must be required in every case where Noor is not recused, we’re at an impasse on corrections.

Noor’s sign-off on the technical finding and final technical wording is a condition of the appointment whenever Noor is responsible for the correction. Finch’s proposed exception leaves us at an impasse, so Noor can’t accept the appointment on those terms.

We propose replacing the adviser, copying, and audit provisions with the following:

**Permitted use and access.** The Testing House may use the drawings and CAD files solely to prepare, conduct, and report on the agreed vibration tests. Access is limited to named test personnel approved in writing by the Design Owner. Before receiving access, each person must be bound by written confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as those in this agreement. The Design Owner may approve personnel changes by email. The Testing House may not disclose the drawings or CAD files to advisers or other third parties or use them, directly or indirectly, to develop or assist in developing competing products.

**Working copies and fixtures.** The Testing House may make encrypted working copies as reasonably necessary for the tests. It may also create test fixtures and fixture files incorporating only the geometry necessary to mount and test the actuator. The same access and use restrictions apply to those copies, fixtures, and files.

**Destruction and verification.** Within 15 business days after the Design Owner accepts the test report or either party terminates the testing engagement, the Testing House must securely delete all drawings and CAD files in its possession or control, including working copies and fixture files, and destroy any fixtures that embody the supplied geometry. The Testing House must provide a written certificate from an independent verifier identifying the materials covered, the destruction methods, and the completion date. The verifier may review inventories and destruction records without receiving the drawings or CAD files. The Design Owner may request supporting records with unrelated confidential information redacted.

We can replace on-demand site access with that certification process. What records would your verifier be able to review, and does your test setup require any fixture geometry beyond the mounting interfaces?

We can work with mounting-interface geometry as the default for fixtures. If test planning identifies a need for additional geometry, we would identify the feature and its purpose and obtain your written approval before extracting or sharing it.

We propose the following wording for the attachments and verification clause.

**Attachment A — Personnel and specialists.** “Attachment A identifies the approved test personnel, specialist machining shop and accredited laboratory, the task assigned to each, and the material each may receive. The shop may receive only the mounting-interface extract needed to machine the fixture. The laboratory may receive only the fixture and the extracts needed to set up and run the tests. Each specialist must limit access to named personnel, apply the same written restrictions on use, copying and destruction, and prohibit onward disclosure. The Testing House remains responsible for each specialist’s compliance.”

**Changes during the job.** “The Testing House may propose a replacement specialist or a change in named personnel by email, identifying the proposed recipient, qualifications, task and access required. The Design Owner will respond within three business days and may withhold approval on reasonable qualification or confidentiality grounds. Email approval updates Attachment A. Before transferring material, the Testing House must bind the replacement to the same restrictions, revoke the outgoing recipient’s access and instruct it to return or destroy its copies.”

**Attachment B — Disposition and retained records.** “Attachment B lists the approved extracts by drawing number and revision, identifies their custodians and records the disposition of each extract, fixture file and physical fixture. The Testing House may retain calibration records for two years, including instrument identifiers, calibration dates and results. Those records must contain no supplied geometry. The existing 15-business-day destruction deadline applies to geometry-bearing materials held by the Testing House and its specialists.”

**Verification.** “By the destruction deadline, the Testing House will provide a certificate signed by its responsible test manager stating the materials covered, destruction methods and completion dates. Supporting evidence will include the Attachment B inventory, access and transfer logs, deletion records, and signed specialist confirmations covering files and physical fixtures as applicable. The Design Owner may request redacted copies. If a specific discrepancy remains after review, a mutually agreed independent verifier may examine the underlying records remotely under confidentiality and report its findings. Would you accept manager certification with independent review for unresolved discrepancies? If you need an independent certificate on every job, we can accommodate a records-only review if we name the verifier in Attachment B before testing and agree who bears the cost.

We can agree to a records-only independent certificate on each job, with the verifier named in Attachment B before testing. We’ll cover the verifier’s fee for the initial review. The Testing House will provide the records and cover any follow-up verification required to correct a documented deficiency in its or a specialist’s destruction or records. The manager’s certificate can form part of the evidence the verifier reviews.

We accept the proposed approach to specialist access, personnel changes and calibration records, with two edits. Attachment A must name each individual who will have access, including at the shop and laboratory, and each must be bound by equivalent written confidentiality, use, copying and destruction obligations before receiving access. For personnel changes, the three-business-day response period is acceptable, with access contingent on express written approval. Before transferring materials to a replacement, the Testing House must revoke the outgoing recipient’s access and obtain written confirmation that any copies were returned or securely destroyed.

We agree that mounting-interface geometry is the default and that any additional geometry requires prior written approval before extraction or disclosure. The test-only use restriction and the express prohibition on using the materials or derivatives to develop or assist in developing competing products apply to all approved recipients.

**Replacement verification clause**

“Within 15 business days after the Design Owner accepts the test report or either party terminates the testing engagement, the Testing House shall complete the required destruction, including for materials held by its specialists, and deliver the independent verifier’s signed certificate to the Design Owner. The verifier shall review the Attachment B inventory, access and transfer logs, deletion records and signed specialist confirmations under written confidentiality obligations. We accept the revised terms for Attachments A and B and the replacement verification clause. We can meet the 15-business-day deadline for destruction and delivery of the independent certificate.

Please include the agreed verifier selection and fee allocation in Attachment B: “Before testing begins, the parties shall name the independent verifier in Attachment B. The Design Owner shall pay the verifier’s fee for the initial review. The Testing House shall provide the review records and pay the cost of follow-up verification required to correct a documented deficiency in its own or a specialist’s destruction or records.”

We propose replacing the blanket approval requirement with the following terms.

- **Trial data.** Raw failure traces and firmware parameters are confidential and may be accessed only by designated members of the parties’ trial teams. Both teams may use other trial measurements internally to run and evaluate the trial, with access limited to personnel who need them for that work.
- **External reports.** Either party may publish aggregate uptime across all three depots, provided the report omits route and depot identifiers and avoids breakdowns that would let readers infer them. The publishing party will give the other party 10 working days to review the draft. If no specific confidentiality concern is raised within that period, publication may proceed. If a concern is raised, the publishing party may proceed once it removes or resolves the material at issue. Other external disclosures of confidential trial data require prior written approval, subject to the safety exception below.
- **Urgent safety.** Either party may disclose the minimum information needed to address an imminent safety risk without prior approval. It will notify the other party as soon as practicable afterward, identifying what was shared and with whom.

What work will the external maintenance contractor perform during the trial? Could it do that work using fault summaries and diagnostic findings from the trial team? If there’s a specific task that requires a raw trace, please identify the task, the fields needed, and why a summary would be insufficient.

The contractor will diagnose faults, repair or replace affected units, and verify that they work before they return to service. We can start with a diagnostic summary containing the unit identifier, fault codes, relevant readings, and the sequence of events expressed in elapsed time. If the summary leaves the cause unclear, the operator’s technical lead can authorize a limited trace excerpt for that repair. For example, distinguishing a brief power interruption from a sensor fault may require the voltage and sensor readings in sequence around the failure. The contractor would receive only the channels and time window needed, under written confidentiality and repair-only use obligations, with access limited to assigned technicians and the excerpt deleted when the repair is closed. Can we make that a standing permission under the NDA, with each release logged by our technical lead?

For routine reporting, our trial lead will prepare a monthly board report covering combined uptime, fault counts, and repair status across the three depots. The operator can circulate that report to the board and its support staff on a confidential basis without further clearance. Board reports and public drafts will omit depot and route identifiers, exact timestamps, and breakdowns that could identify a depot or employee. If the board report will be made public, the publication terms apply.

Your 10-working-day review works for publication of combined uptime. The publishing party’s designated lead approves release after the review period if no specific confidentiality concern is raised. If a concern is raised, the lead may release the draft once the disputed material has been removed or both parties’ designated leads agree in writing on how to address it. Publication of other confidential trial data requires both parties’ written approval.

The safety exception also needs to cover prompt reporting of serious incidents to the appropriate authorities, including when the immediate danger has passed. Either party’s safety lead may make those reports, or disclose information needed to address an imminent risk, without prior notice or approval. The disclosure is limited to what the authority requires or what is reasonably needed for the safety response. The disclosing party will tell the other party what was shared and with whom as soon as practicable afterward, to the extent permitted.

We can give the contractor standing access to diagnostic summaries for assigned repairs. If a summary is inconclusive, the operator’s technical lead can request a targeted analysis from the trial team. For the power interruption example, the team can compare the voltage and sensor channels and provide the timing and duration of any voltage drop, how it lines up with the sensor fault, and what to check before returning the unit to service.

We propose the following contractor clause.

> The operator’s technical lead may disclose to assigned contractor technicians the diagnostic information reasonably needed to diagnose, repair or replace a trial unit and verify its operation. This may include the unit identifier, fault codes, selected readings, an elapsed-time event summary and findings from the trial team’s analysis. Raw failure traces, including excerpts, and firmware parameters remain accessible only to designated trial team members, subject to the safety exception. The contractor must be bound in writing to keep the information confidential, use it only for the assigned work, limit access to assigned technicians and delete the diagnostic material when the repair is closed. The technical lead will log what was shared, with whom and for which repair.

If the trial team can review the underlying channels and relay its findings while the repair is open, is there a return-to-service check the contractor must perform itself that still requires the original sequence? If so, please identify the check so we can agree on how the trial team will support it.

We accept confidential circulation of the monthly report to the board and support staff who need it for board business, without further clearance. The report may include combined uptime, fault counts and repair status across all three depots, with the exclusions you proposed.

The publishing party’s designated lead may approve release if no specific confidentiality concern is raised within that period. If a concern is raised, the lead may approve release once the disputed material is removed or both designated leads agree in writing on how to address it. Either party’s safety lead may report a serious incident to the appropriate authorities, including after the immediate danger has passed, or disclose information needed to address an imminent safety risk, without prior notice or approval. The disclosure is limited to what the authority requires or what is reasonably needed for the safety response. The disclosing party will tell the other party what was shared and with whom as soon as practicable afterward, to the extent permitted.

We can accept the contractor clause as drafted. The contractor can verify operation using live readings and an agreed functional test. Let’s add one operating provision: “Before the trial begins, each party will name a technical contact and a backup for requests that affect return to service. With that addition, we can finalize the contractor, monthly board reporting, publication approval, and urgent safety terms as set out in your message.

For a scan held for an open correction, that period starts when the studio deletes the active copy upon redelivery. A restore does not restart the clock.
